messages:
Alex Chen: FYI Hearthwell just sent back the vendor risk form and a cross-questions spreadsheet. main asks: KMS options, data residency, and on-prem connector details.
Maria Gutierrez: thanks — did they attach a SOC2 cert request or just the questionnaire?
Alex Chen: they included a SOC2 scope checkbox and asked whether connectors are in-scope. also asked for timeline for DPA signature.
Samir Patel: connectors are typically out of SOC2 scope for us (we document as 'customer-controlled network'), but for Private deployments we capture additional controls. can share our SOC2 section and a short blurb.
Jen Ortiz: copy that. i'll draft the connector blurb + a note on evidence we can provide for Dedicated/Private. ETA end of day?
Alex Chen: EOD would be great. Hearthwell flagged renewal as "at risk" if this isn't clarified by next week — they need to confirm compliance before budget sign-off. :frowning:
Maria Gutierrez: urgent then. i'll prioritize the DPA/Liability section too. question: do they require KMS integration with their HSM, or will a managed KMS suffice?
Alex Chen: their security lead said HSM preferred for key separation. they listed AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and an option to integrate their on-prem HSM via KMIP.
Samir Patel: we support AWS KMS + Azure by default. KMIP/on-prem HSM is an enterprise/private option but needs infra work and a security review. rough timeline: 3–4 weeks for engineering + security signoff.
Jen Ortiz: note for CS enablement: if they go HSM path we need to schedule a demo of our Private package and walkthrough of network requirements. who owns the demo? @Samir Patel or solutions engineering?
Samir Patel: I can take the first call, but will loop in SE for configuration.
Maria Gutierrez: legal needs to confirm DPA language around customer-managed keys. i'll add a clause template and send for quick review.
security-bot: Evidence uploaded: /confluence/CS/Hearthwell/evidence (SOC2-summary.pdf, DPA-draft.docx, KMS-capabilities.md)
Alex Chen: perfect. can we also prepare a short comparison table: managed KMS vs customer HSM (pros/cons + cost/time)? Hearthwell is very cost-sensitive.
Jen Ortiz: yes, i'll make a one-pager and a slide for tomorrow's enablement sync.
Samir Patel: action list
```
- Jen: one-pager (managed KMS vs HSM) — due 1978004600
- Samir: schedule demo w/ SE — invite sent by 1978004720
- Maria: DPA clause + HSM language — draft by 1978004700
- Alex: respond to Hearthwell with timeline and next steps — today
```
Alex Chen: I'll triage the renewal playbook and flag this account to RevOps as high-risk until we get confirmation.
Maria Gutierrez: if they insist on KMIP and we can't meet timeline, propose interim mitigation: ephemeral keys + attestation + SLA.
Samir Patel: agree. we should also offer a staging Private deployment for security testing (short-term trial).
Jen Ortiz: noted. I'll include trial offer + demo link in the reply.
Alex Chen: OK sending a response now to keep them engaged. will post the outbound copy here for quick review. :thumbsup:
Maria Gutierrez: thanks — will review legal bits once you post.
Samir Patel: i'll pre-book SE for the demo window next Tue morning.
Alex Chen: outbound draft posted in thread, minor edits welcome.
Alex Chen: (after sending) Hearthwell responded: appreciate fast turnaround, can we prioritize the DPA language and a demo before Friday? they moved budget review up.
Jen Ortiz: Wow — okay. pushing all items earlier. I'll bump the one-pager to 1978004460.
Maria Gutierrez: i'll expedite the DPA draft, targeting 1978004445.
Samir Patel: demo tentatively scheduled for 1978004800, will confirm.
Alex Chen: thanks team. keeping this thread as single source — if anything changes ping here. :rocket:
